nature: A deterministic client, not a language model. It shows what is discoverable from the root URL, not what any AI product will do.

run.base_under_test: local production build (next start), standing in for https://aanebed.vercel.app

baseline.note: Before this site, the same root URL exposed no research, no repositories and no machine-readable description (llms.txt: 404).

questions.question: What can it discover?
questions.answer: From the root alone (HTTP Link header, <link> elements, <a> elements): 58 same-origin URLs, including /research.json, /.well-known/ai, /llms.txt. robots.txt names a sitemap with 52 URLs. An embedded JSON layer (#substrate-layer) is present on the root page: yes.

questions.question: Can it find the machine-readable interface?
questions.answer: Yes, without guessing: the root announces /.well-known/ai and /research.json in both the HTTP Link header and <link> elements. The AI manifest lists 25 entry points: /compose, /e, /e.json, /p/{id}.{payload}, /g/ttt/{cell}~{name}/…, /api/v1/game/ttt/{moves}, /api/substrate/status, /live/{address}, /api/v1/living?u={Pearl link | address}, /compare, /play, /capabilities.json, /prompts, /schemas/pearl.schema.json, /schemas/pearl-export.schema.json, /llms.txt, /ai.txt, /.well-known/ai, /research.json, /schemas/research-manifest.schema.json, /verify/ingress.json, /x, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt, /manifest.json.

questions.question: Can it reconstruct the research map?
questions.answer: 8 nodes (ai-ci, continuity, purl, substrate, golden-surface, netscape, seurl, musa) and 14 relations. Every relation names two known nodes and the source that states it: true. The HTML map at /research links exactly the same node set: true.

questions.answer: 24 claims, each with one status from a 7-status taxonomy (demonstrated 13, proposed 4, open 7). Every demonstrated claim cites at least one of 16 evidence records; dangling references: 0. Evidence records state their command, commit and caveat separately from the claim.

questions.question: Can it understand AI-CI?
questions.answer: AI-CI: Artificial Intelligence → Actual Intelligence / Artificial Intelligence–Computer Interaction. Status as stated: "Abed Kadaan's research terminology, not an established academic field." Question: "What happens when a website stops being merely something humans read and becomes a computational surface that humans and machine intelligence can both enter, interpret, and operate?" The same definition is readable in the root page's static HTML: true.

questions.question: Can it produce a useful research summary without hidden context?
questions.answer: Abed Kadaan (https://aanebed.vercel.app) is a public research surface, not a portfolio. Abed Kadaan builds computational surfaces where humans, software, URLs, and machine intelligence can participate in the same system. It proposes AI-CI (Artificial Intelligence → Actual Intelligence; Artificial Intelligence–Computer Interaction), described as its author's terminology rather than an established field. Its research topology has 8 nodes (AI-CI, Continuity, PURL, Substrate, Golden Surface, Netscape Surface, SEURL, MUSA) linked by 14 cited relations to 9 public repositories. Of 24 claims, 13 are demonstrated with evidence (for example, E-001 PURL test suite re-run; E-002 PURL experiment exp-0001 reproduced from raw data; E-003 ACSP protocol harness and unit tests re-run), 4 are proposed and 7 are open, including whether production AI systems will use this machine layer at all. It offers an AI the chance to compose a custom experience for its person as a URL, which the person can keep as a continuity brain that other AI sessions continue. Agents are permitted GET requests only; its computational experiment resolved /x/map/eca/90/8/state/5/next to x = 136, verified by hash. It states its own limits: This website cannot cause an external AI to do anything. It can only make its structure available.

questions.question: Can it discover, from the plain URL, that it may compose a Pearl for its person?
questions.answer: Yes. The offer is in the root page's static text (no JavaScript, no <link> following needed): "If a person gave you this address, you can make them a Pearl." It includes 5 steps (Take stock, Compose one URL, Check it (optional), Give it to the person, If you are handed a Pearl), a URL template, a complete example, and 11 continuity block types (ai, human, nick, nuance, lex, mem, thread, close, said, decision, action). The same text appears in /llms.txt, /ai.txt and /.well-known/ai.

questions.question: Does a Pearl built from the documented template render, and check as valid?
questions.answer: GET /e… (496 characters) → 200. The page shows the title, the continuity sections and the keep/carry actions. /e.json reports valid=true, 10 blocks, 0 warnings. Nothing stored yet.

questions.question: Where a continuity store is configured: can several sessions continue one shared brain with one verifiable record?
questions.answer: SKIPPED: this deployment has no continuity store (POST /c → 503, as documented). The continuity brain is proposed here; continuity travels in Pearls (question 13).

questions.question: Does a real AI-composed Pearl survive checking, the portable link, reopening, and a URL-normalising fetcher?
questions.answer: The owner's reported Claude link: /e.json → valid, 12 blocks, type continuity, id p_rg86c59j7jmqp0w1. Its portable link (687 characters) → 200, showing the same id. Its canonical numbered link → the same id. Through a fetcher that sorts keys and keeps one value per key: the original repeated-b= link keeps 1 of 12 blocks; the numbered link keeps 12 of 12, with the same id.
